text:
Asha: Heads-up — since ~03:40UTC otel-collector-01 CPU jumped to ~85% and our app p99 for request processing went from ~230ms -> ~760ms. Traces show exporter queueing/backpressure. Anyone seeing this?
Mike: saw similar in grafana, span ingest rate doubled after the deploy at 03:25. hard to tell if exporter or span churn.
Olivia: exporter gRPC send latency p99 ~900ms on the collector pod logs. backlog length spiking.
Sanjay: ingest-bot alert fired: otel-collector CPU high on shard-3 and exporter queue size > 50k.
ingest-bot: ALERT: otel-collector.cpu > 70% (shard-3) — link: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/OTEL-CPU-1809
Mike: can we see a snippet of the collector pipeline? especially processors.batch config and otlp exporter settings.
Asha: pasted minimal relevant parts below:
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 5s
    send_batch_size: 200
exporters:
  otlp/remote:
    endpoint: ingest.kafka-proxy:4317
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
```
Olivia: send_batch_size 200 is pretty small given our bursty traffic — that can cause a lot of CPU churn with many exporter RPCs. increasing batch size or timeout should amortize overhead.
Sanjay: also noticed a surprising span count per request on checkout path — ~45 spans/request where previously it was ~8. instrumentation loop in payments service creating per-line-item spans.
Mike: oh that explains it. more spans *and* small batches = exporter saturated. two levers: reduce span volume (remove low-value spans) + bump batch settings.
Asha: proposed quick mitigation: 1) patch payments service to stop instrumenting per-item DB hits (PR ready), 2) increase batch.timeout to 10s and send_batch_size to 1000 for a canary, 3) enable probabilistic sampling (0.2) on high-throughput services.
Olivia: agree. canary plan: 2% of collectors first, watch exporter rpc latency, collector CPU, and app p99. If stable, ramp 20% -> 100% over 2h.
Sanjay: also trimming high-cardinality attributes from Redis spans will reduce size and CPU for marshalling.
Mike: added quick config diff to the canary branch:
```diff
 processors:
-  batch:
-    timeout: 5s
-    send_batch_size: 200
+  batch:
+    timeout: 10s
+    send_batch_size: 1000
```
Asha: created ticket RED-3421 and linked the PR: https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-3421 — includes rollback steps and dashboards to watch (collector_cpu, otlp_rpc_p99, trace_backlog).
Olivia: starting the canary config rollout to 2% now. will attach dashboard links shortly.
ingest-bot: deploy started: otel-collector-config-canary -> shard-3 (2%) 
Mike: monitoring graphs look better within 3min for the canary node — exporter p99 dropped from ~900ms -> ~120ms and CPU down ~30%.
Sanjay: good catch. still want to merge the instrumentation change ASAP to avoid hitting quotas or storage explosion.
Asha: agreed. PR for payments instrumentation has tests and is in review; I'll ping @payments on the PR.
Olivia: after we confirm stability at 20% I'll also propose adding a minimal tail-based sampler for checkout path so we don't lose important traces but cut volume.
Mike: +1. follow-up: add a load test that simulates 60 spans/request to ensure collector scaling. filed as RED-3422.
Asha: thanks team — keeping this thread for postmortem notes. I'll update RED-3421 with timeline and mitigation. :thumbsup:
